chief_complaint: trouble peeing and lower belly pain
hpi_details: 70M presents with 2 days of worsening difficulty urinating. Today he has been unable to pass any urine for 12 hours and has severe lower abdominal discomfort and fullness.
medications: Tamsulosin, newly started over-the-counter cold medicine (Diphenhydramine)

investigation_events.title: Urgent urinary retention assessment
investigation_events.availability_message: Bedside bladder scan and urgent renal function results are now available. Bladder decompression should not be delayed while awaiting blood tests.

core_concepts: Commonly caused by BPH in older men, often triggered by anticholinergic or sympathomimetic medications (like OTC cold meds).
Can cause post-renal acute kidney injury (AKI).
common_misconceptions: Assuming anuria is due to a kidney problem (pre-renal/intrinsic) without checking bladder volume.
dangerous_errors: Failing to decompress the bladder promptly, leading to permanent detrusor damage or severe AKI.
management_principles: Immediate bladder ultrasound, placement of Foley catheter, check BMP for AKI, stop offending meds.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

source_refs.title: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for Kidney Disease

reference_soap.subjective: 70M with BPH presenting with acute inability to void for 12 hours and suprapubic pain after taking cold medicine.
reference_soap.objective: Distended, tender suprapubic mass. Bladder scan shows >999 mL.
reference_soap.assessment: Acute urinary retention, likely medication-induced superimposed on BPH.
reference_soap.plan: STAT Foley catheter placement. Check BMP. Stop diphenhydramine. Follow up with urology.

learning_objectives: Recognize acute urinary retention and identify common medication triggers.

teaching.one_liner: Acute inability to void with a painful, distended bladder in an elderly man, often triggered by anticholinergic medications.

must_ask.say: When did you last pass urine, and how has your urine stream been recently?
Have you had any trouble starting your stream, dribbling, or waking at night to urinate before this?
Have you taken any cold or allergy medicine, or other new medications recently?
How severe is the lower belly pain, and does it come with an urge to void?
Have you had any back pain, leg weakness, or numbness that could point to a nerve problem?

history.answer: I haven't been able to pee at all since this morning, and my lower belly is in terrible pain and feels completely full.
My main trouble is that no urine will come out at all, not that it is leaking.
It started getting noticeably harder to pee two days ago, and starting twelve hours ago this morning, it stopped coming out entirely.
Over the past few months I have had to wait a while for the stream to start, and the flow was weak, but I could usually push it out until today.
Yes, I usually feel like I haven't completely emptied my bladder, and urine often dribbles onto my pants after I finish.
I have not passed a single drop of urine for twelve hours, and my lower belly is swollen, tight, and aching intensely.
history.topic: Complete inability to void and lower belly pain

history.answer: Usually I go to the bathroom six or seven times during the day and wake up three or four times at night to pee.
I often get a sudden, strong urge to go where I have to hurry, but I haven't had accidents where urine leaked before I reached the toilet.
No, I never leak when coughing, laughing, sneezing, or lifting heavy objects, and I have never worn pads.
It burned a little bit when I was trying to strain yesterday, but I haven't seen any blood in my urine and I have had no fever or chills.
No, I do not have back pain, leg weakness, numbness, loss of feeling around my bottom, or bowel leakage.
No, my bowels have been moving regularly, and I had a normal bowel movement yesterday.
I usually drink around four glasses of water and one cup of coffee a day, but I stopped drinking fluids today because the fullness is unbearable.
I caught a bad head cold two days ago, so I started taking an over-the-counter nighttime cold medicine containing diphenhydramine for the last two nights.
No, I have never had diabetes, a stroke, Parkinson's disease, or any spine surgery.
No, I have never injured my groin, never had a catheter or urinary procedure, and never had any sexually transmitted infections or urethritis.
My doctor diagnosed me with an enlarged prostate, or benign prostatic hyperplasia, about three years ago.
The pain is a severe, constant aching pressure in the middle of my lower belly, about an eight out of ten, and it hurts worse when pressed.
I think my enlarged prostate has swollen up so much that it completely shut off the urine passage.
The pressure is so unbearable that I am genuinely terrified my bladder is going to burst.
Please put in a catheter or tube right away to drain the urine; I desperately need relief.
Apart from the enlarged prostate, I have mild high blood pressure, but no other chronic illnesses.
I had my appendix removed when I was a teenager, but I have had no other surgeries and no hospital stays since then.
I take tamsulosin daily for my prostate, and I started that over-the-counter diphenhydramine cold medicine two nights ago.
No, I do not have any allergies to medications, foods, or latex.
I smoked half a pack a day in my twenties, but I quit completely over thirty years ago.
I only drink an occasional beer once or twice a month, and none recently.
I am a retired accountant, and I live at home with my wife.
My father had prostate enlargement as he aged, but there is no family history of prostate cancer or kidney failure.

exam.finding: The patient is an elderly male appearing in marked discomfort, grimacing and holding his lower abdomen.
Blood pressure 142/88 mmHg, pulse 86 beats/min, respiratory rate 18 breaths/min, temperature 36.8°C, oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
Visible fullness and distension in the suprapubic midline with no surgical scars.
A smooth, firm, tensely distended and tender suprapubic mass is palpable extending halfway up to the umbilicus; no guarding or rigidity elsewhere.
Dullness to percussion over the palpable suprapubic mass, with normal tympany elsewhere in the abdomen.
Normal anal sphincter tone; symmetrically enlarged, smooth, rubbery prostate with no nodules or tenderness.
Normal 5/5 motor strength in all muscle groups of the bilateral lower extremities.
Intact light touch sensation across bilateral lower extremities and normal perianal saddle sensation.
Patellar and Achilles tendon reflexes are 2+ bilaterally, with downward plantar reflexes.
